deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: A description of this sink. The maximum length of the description is 8000 characters.
description.rationale: Description is metadata only and does not affect any security controls.

destination.description: The destination of the sink (or, in other words, where logs are written to). Can be a Cloud Storage bucket, a PubSub topic, or a BigQuery dataset. Examples: "storage.googleapis.com/[GCS_BUCKET]" "bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/datasets/[DATASET]" "pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/topics/[TOPIC_ID]" The writer associated with the sink must have access to write to the above resource.
destination.rationale: Identifies the external resource the sink writes logs to (a Cloud Storage bucket, Pub/Sub topic, or BigQuery dataset). This is a reference to another resource; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific approved project/bucket names, which is overreaching. We secure this resource's own config, not the names of resources it points at.

disabled.description: If set to True, then this sink is disabled and it does not export any log entries.
disabled.rationale: If disabled is set to true, log export stops working. Disabling critical log sinks can break security monitoring, compliance reporting, and incident response capabilities.

filter.description: The filter to apply when exporting logs. Only log entries that match the filter are exported.
filter.rationale: Filter determines which logs are exported. Overly restrictive filters can exclude critical security logs (audit logs, IAM changes, firewall changes), creating blind spots for security monitoring and incident response.

folder.description: The folder to be exported to the sink. Note that either [FOLDER_ID] or "folders/[FOLDER_ID]" is accepted.
folder.rationale: This identifies which folder owns the sink. It has no direct security impact on the sink's behavior.

include_children.description: Whether or not to include children folders in the sink export. If true, logs associated with child projects are also exported; otherwise only logs relating to the provided folder are included.
include_children.rationale: When set to false, logs from child projects may not be exported, creating gaps in security monitoring coverage. For complete visibility, should be set to true unless there are specific organizational requirements to exclude child project logs.

intercept_children.description: Whether or not to intercept logs from child projects. If true, matching logs will not match with sinks in child resources, except _Required sinks. This sink will be visible to child resources when listing sinks.
intercept_children.rationale: When set to true, this sink can override child sinks, potentially bypassing their exclusions or filters. Should be used carefully to ensure child-level security controls are not unintentionally bypassed.

name.description: The name of the logging sink.
name.rationale: Name is a unique identifier for the sink. It has no security implications beyond being a reference name.

bigquery_options.description: Options that affect sinks exporting data to BigQuery.

bigquery_options.use_partitioned_tables.description: Whether to use BigQuery's partition tables. By default, Logging creates dated tables based on the log entries' timestamps, e.g. syslog_20170523. With partitioned tables the date suffix is no longer present and special query syntax has to be used instead. In both cases, tables are sharded based on UTC timezone.
bigquery_options.use_partitioned_tables.rationale: Partitioned tables improve query performance and cost management but have no security implications.

exclusions.description: Log entries that match any of the exclusion filters will not be exported. If a log entry is matched by both filter and one of exclusion's filters, it will not be exported.

exclusions.description.rationale: Description is metadata only and does not affect security controls.

exclusions.disabled.description: If set to True, then this exclusion is disabled and it does not exclude any log entries
exclusions.disabled.rationale: Toggles whether this sink-level exclusion actively drops matching log entries from export. The security-relevant control is the exclusion filter content (assessed separately); whether a given exclusion is enabled is a team data-management choice and disabling it only retains more logs, so a generic policy on this toggle adds no security value.

exclusions.filter.description: An advanced logs filter that matches the log entries to be excluded. By using the sample function, you can exclude less than 100% of the matching log entries
exclusions.filter.rationale: Filter determines which logs are excluded from export. Excluding audit logs, IAM changes, or high severity logs creates critical security blind spots.

exclusions.name.description: A client-assigned identifier, such as "load-balancer-exclusion". Identifiers are limited to 100 characters and can include only letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, and periods. First character has to be alphanumeric.
exclusions.name.rationale: Name is a unique identifier for the exclusion. Has no security implications.
